title: Schema Contract Explorer and Parameter Fixplaybook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a robust, discoverable JSON schema contract explorer and an accompanying 'fixplaybook' to reduce developer friction when function/tool calls fail validation. This ticket scopes: UI + API surface for schema inspection, canonical validation error taxonomy, automated remediation hints (fixplaybook), and a compatibility shim for legacy tool manifests. Out of scope: runtime kernel-level kernel optimizations or batcher changes (these are covered by serving-runtime epics).
problem_statement: Customers and internal SDKs are repeatedly tripping over subtle parameter mismatches: wrong field types, missing required fields, ambiguous optional unions, and extant legacy manifests that omit schema versioning. Current errors are low-signal, causing long debug loops and support tickets. We need a first-class explorer and a prescriptive remediation workflow to reduce mean time to resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Expose a read-only /schemas/{tool_id} HTTP endpoint that returns the canonical JSON schema plus a human-friendly summary
Implement an error taxonomy with stable error codes surfaced in validation responses (e.g., VAL-MISSING-REQ, VAL-TYPE-MISMATCH, VAL-UNKNOWN-FIELD, VAL-UNION-AMBIGUITY)
Server returns validation payload with 'hints' array containing 1-3 prioritized remediation suggestions when validation fails
Console shows inline schema explorer for tools with collapsible field descriptions, examples, and sample payload generator
Compatibility shim runs for manifests tagged with schema_version < 2 and emits deprecation telemetry and suggested conversion steps
Automated unit tests covering 90% of validation branching (missing required, extra fields, coercion), and end-to-end test calling a staging runtime showing improved error messages in SDKs
API contract and docs published in team Confluence and linked from SDK error pages
tasks: Design API spec and error code list (doc: confluence/redwood/tool-schema-explorer)
Backend: add /schemas/{tool_id} and refactor validator to emit structured errors and hints
Backend: implement compatibility shim for schema_version < 2 with mapping rules
Console: embed schema explorer widget and sample request builder
SDK: surface validation error codes and include 'fixplaybook' hints in thrown exceptions
Telemetry: add metric validation.failures_by_code and event with tool_id, user_id, schema_version
Write unit + integration tests; update CI to run schema contract test matrix
Docs: author migration guide for partners with legacy manifests
notes_or_decisions: Decision: Use JSON Schema Draft-07 as the canonical syntax for the explorer. We will add a lightweight 'x-example' and 'x-semantic' extension fields to capture semantic hints and preferred examples.
Decision: Error codes must be stable strings (VAL-*) rather than HTTP-only messages so SDKs can map behavior deterministically.
Trade-off: We will avoid introducing a new DSL to reduce cognitive overhead; instead extend JSON Schema with 'x-' fields for human guidance.
Performance note: Validator will run in the request pre-validator path; keep checks bounded and run expensive deep-coercion only when caller opts into 'fix_suggestions=true'.
Compatibility policy: For schema_version < 2, shim will attempt safe renames and optional field coercion; irreversible structural changes will emit a 'manual migration required' hint.
Telemetry retention: keep validation failure events for 90 days in analytics to spot common pain points for prioritization.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API + validator): backend schema endpoint and structured error payloads. Phase 2 (Console + SDK): explorer UI and SDK integration for mapped error codes. Phase 3 (Compatibility + rollout): migration shim, telemetry dashboards, and gradual opt-in with feature flag. Rollout uses canary on 5% of traffic for two weeks before full release.
compatibility_examples: Legacy manifest: {manifest_version: 1, params: [{name: "text", type: "string"}] } -> shim suggestion: rename 'params' to 'properties' and wrap in 'input' object
Ambiguous union: when schema allows [string, object], validator will return VAL-UNION-AMBIGUITY with hint to add a discriminator field or prefer 'coerce_to_string' option
risks: Backend validator bloat: duplicate logic between runtime and policy-checker increases maintenance cost
Overly prescriptive hints could encourage brittle client behavior; mitigate by including confidence score and 'non-binding' flag
Console UX complexity if schemas are deeply nested; need progressive disclosure and example-driven guidance
